scenes.text: It's the summer of 1720, and the smartest man in Europe is buying back into a bubble.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: You discovered the laws of gravity. You invented a new kind of mathematics.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: And right now, you're buying shares in the South Sea Company at the highest price ever.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: A few months ago, you sold those same shares, at a nice profit.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: Then you watched your friends get richer. So you're back in, with much more money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: By winter, you'll have lost a fortune: more than most people earn in a lifetime.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you here, and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's Christmas Day, 1642, and you're born in Lincolnshire.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Your name is Isaac Newton. Keep count of two things: the money, and the enemies.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your father, also called Isaac, died three months before you were born.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're born so early and so small, your mother says you'd fit in a quart mug.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When you're three, she marries a rich old minister, Barnabas Smith, and moves out.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: She leaves you behind with your grandmother.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You don't take it well.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Years later, you write a list of your sins, and one of them stands out.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: THREATENING TO BURN THEM AND THE HOUSE

scenes.text: Threatening my father and mother Smith to burn them and the house over them.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Threatening my father and mother Smith to burn them and the house over them.

scenes.text: You keep lists of everything, even your own sins. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When you're ten, your stepfather dies, and your mother comes home with three new children.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: apothecary's shop in Grantham, 1650s: shelves of jars and bottles, herbs drying, a wooden counter

scenes.text: At twelve you go to school in Grantham. A windmill model. Sundials. A kite with a lantern that scares the neighbors at night.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At sixteen, your mother pulls you out of school.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You're going to run the family farm.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: You are a terrible farmer. You read books while the sheep wander off.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: The local court fines you because your animals broke into a neighbor's fields.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Remember that: you can't even manage a few sheep.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Your old schoolmaster begs your mother to send you to university. She gives in.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: In 1661, you arrive at Trinity College, Cambridge, as a subsizar: a student who works as a servant.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: You empty richer students' chamber pots to pay your way.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: Your mother has money. She just doesn't send much of it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: You win a scholarship in 1664, and then the plague arrives.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: The university shuts down, and you go home to the farm for about two years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Alone, with no teachers, you start working out calculus, light and gravity.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: And yes, there's an apple.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: The internet says it fell on your head. It didn't.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Decades later, you tell a friend you saw an apple fall in the garden, and wondered why straight down.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: No bump on the head. Just a man staring at fruit for a very long time.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Woolsthorpe Manor farmhouse in Lincolnshire, 1650s: small grey stone house, apple tree in the garden, sheep in a field, low stone wall, overcast sky

scenes.text: Back in Cambridge, you become a professor at twenty-six.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: Your lectures are so hard that sometimes nobody comes, and you lecture to the walls.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: You buy prisms at a fair and split sunlight into colors in your darkened room.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: To study vision, you push a blunt needle behind your own eyeball, and write down what you see.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: Yes, you take notes. Of course you take notes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: Secretly, you also spend years on alchemy: trying to turn cheap metals into gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You never manage it. But gold is about to become your job anyway.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In London, a scientist named Robert Hooke criticizes your work on light.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: You write him a famous letter.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

quote.text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.

scenes.text: It sounds humble. Hooke was very short. Some historians think that was the joke.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: Either way, you hate each other for the rest of his life. Enemy number one.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: In 1684, the astronomer Edmond Halley visits you with a question about planets.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: You tell him you've already solved it. You just lost the paper.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: He talks you into writing the whole thing down. It becomes the Principia.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: One problem. The Royal Society has spent its printing money on a book about fish.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: The fish book flopped. So Halley pays to print your book himself.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: The Society even pays Halley's salary in unsold copies of the fish book.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Society meeting room in London, 1680s: long table with a green cloth, globes, telescopes, a pile of printed books, tall windows

scenes.text: In 1687, the Principia explains gravity, the tides and the planets.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: You're famous. You're still not rich.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: The bubble that costs you a fortune is thirty-three years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: student room at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1660s: wooden desk with candles, prisms and books, a window with a beam of sunlight, narrow bed

scenes.text: Now, a money problem that's about to become your job.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small market stall with a coin box

scenes.text: English silver coins in the 1690s are made by hand, with plain edges.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So people shave a little silver off the edges, melt it, and sell it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's called clipping. Do it to every coin you touch, and you get rich slowly.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Imagine two kinds of gift card. One is full. One has had money shaved off it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Shops have to treat both cards the same. Which one would you spend?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The shaved one. You keep the full one at home.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Soon only shaved cards are in circulation. The good ones vanish.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's Gresham's law: bad money drives out good money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By 1695, many English coins have lost close to half their silver.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Prices go up, trade gets messy, and nobody trusts a shilling.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1696, a friend in government, Charles Montagu, offers you a job: Warden of the Royal Mint.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: It's meant to be an easy, well-paid job for a famous man.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: Remember the boy who couldn't manage sheep? He's now helping run England's money factory.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: And he takes it very seriously.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: England is replacing all its old silver coins in one go: the Great Recoinage.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: New coins get milled edges, the little ridges, so clipping shows right away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: You learn the furnaces, the presses, the cost of every step.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: While the old coins are melted down, there's hardly any money to pay wages with.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: You push the presses to run day and night until the new coins come out.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: You estimate that one coin in five coming in is fake.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: Counterfeiting is high treason. The punishment is death.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: And the Warden's job includes catching the counterfeiters. Most wardens don't bother. You do.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Mint inside the Tower of London, 1696: heavy screw presses for stamping coins, furnaces, sacks of silver, stone walls, lanterns

scenes.text: You build a network of informers in London's taverns.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: Some accounts say you went in disguise yourself. Nobody knows how often.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: Remember the boy who wrote down every sin? Now you write down everyone else's.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: You run more than a hundred interrogations in about eighteen months.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: Your biggest target is William Chaloner, the best counterfeiter in England.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: He makes fake coins, fake banknotes, and lives like a gentleman.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: A few years earlier, he turned in some printers of illegal pamphlets, and collected a thousand-pound reward.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: Some say he'd helped set the printers up in the first place.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: He's a man who makes money from crime, and then makes money from reporting crime.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: He even tells Parliament the Mint is incompetent, and offers to run it better.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: That makes him enemy number two.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: You spend a year gathering witnesses against him.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rough London tavern, 1698: low wooden beams, barrels, tankards on sticky tables, a fireplace, dim candlelight

scenes.text: In 1699, he's convicted of high treason.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

scenes.text: From his cell he writes to you, begging.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

scenes.text: O dear Sir, nobody can save me but you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

quote.text: O dear Sir, nobody can save me but you.

scenes.text: You don't answer. In March 1699, Chaloner is hanged.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

scenes.text: Enemy number two, gone. You file the paperwork.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

scenes.text: You prosecute twenty-eight coiners in total. The money gets better.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Newgate Prison cell in London, 1699: damp stone walls, straw on the floor, iron chains on the wall, a small barred window, a wooden stool

scenes.text: At the end of 1699 you become Master of the Mint, the top job.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Master gets a cut of every coin made. In good years, that's well over a thousand pounds.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: For the first time in your life, you're rich.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Since 1696 you've lived in a fine house on Jermyn Street in London.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: Your half-niece, Catherine Barton, runs the house and charms your guests.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: London says she's the most charming woman in town. You never marry.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: In 1705, Queen Anne knights you. You're Sir Isaac now.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: Historians think it was mostly about winning an election, not about gravity.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: Then enemy number three appears: Gottfried Leibniz, a German genius.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: He published calculus first. You worked it out first, but kept it in a drawer.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: You're now President of the Royal Society, so it sets up a committee to decide who was right.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The committee's report says you were. You wrote the report yourself.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Historians today say both of you invented calculus, separately.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that list of sins? This one probably didn't make it on.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1717, you write a report on gold coins, and the government sets a guinea at twenty-one shillings.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: You set gold a little too high, so silver quietly leaves the country.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: Remember Gresham's law? Britain ends up on a gold standard, by accident or not.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: elegant London townhouse parlour on Jermyn Street, 1710: wood-panelled walls, portraits, a writing desk with letters, a fireplace, crimson curtains

scenes.text: Now we're back where we started. 1720, Exchange Alley.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: The South Sea Company has a monopoly on trade with South America, and almost no trade.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: What it does have is a deal to take over the government's debt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: Its shares go from about one hundred pounds in January to about one thousand in June.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: Remember the planets you calculated? This is harder.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: You own shares already. In the spring, you sell them, and make a solid profit.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Jonathan's Coffee House in Exchange Alley, London, 1720: crowded wooden benches, chalk boards of share prices (blank), coffee pots, papers on tables, smoky light

scenes.text: Then the price keeps going up. And up. Without you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Everyone you know is getting richer. Catherine's friends. Your neighbors. Strangers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Copycat companies pop up every week, selling shares in almost anything.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: One famous story says a company sold shares in an undertaking of great advantage, nobody to know what it is.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That one might be a legend. The craze around it is not.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In June, Parliament passes the Bubble Act to stop the copycats. Nobody stops buying.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So in the summer, you buy back in, near the top, with much more money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You picture your money growing like the shares in the papers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In September, the bubble bursts. The shares fall back toward one hundred.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You lose at least ten thousand pounds, and probably more than twenty thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's millions in today's money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The internet says you sighed: I can calculate the motions of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That line comes from a secondhand story, written down years later. You may never have said it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your relatives say you couldn't bear to hear the words South Sea for the rest of your life.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You keep working at the Mint into your eighties.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: You still check the coins, the accounts and the counterfeiters, line by line.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: Your health fails slowly: kidney stones, coughing, and pain you rarely complain about.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: Catherine and her husband, John Conduitt, look after you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: Conduitt writes down your stories, including the one about the apple.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: On March 20th, 1727, you die in Kensington, aged eighty-four.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: Even after the bubble, you leave about thirty thousand pounds.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: You leave no will. Your relatives split the money, and argue over your papers for years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: Among those papers are about a million words on alchemy, hidden for two centuries.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: bedroom in a Kensington house, 1727: four-poster bed with heavy curtains, medicine bottles on a side table, candle, quiet evening light

scenes.text: You're buried in Westminster Abbey, the first scientist ever buried there.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight

scenes.text: A young French writer, Voltaire, is in London and watches it all.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight

scenes.text: He writes that you never had a passion in your life.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight

quote.text: He was never sensible to any passion.

scenes.text: He clearly never saw your list of sins.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight

scenes.text: The poet Alexander Pope writes your most famous epitaph.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight

paper.text: GOD SAID, LET NEWTON BE! AND ALL WAS LIGHT

scenes.text: So how does the man who explained gravity lose a fortune to a bubble?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He didn't lose it by being dumb. He lost it by watching other people get rich.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Selling was the smart move. Buying back in because of his neighbors was the mistake.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That brings us to today's money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: DON'T CHASE WHAT YOU SOLD

scenes.bgIdea: modern bank branch, 2020s

scenes.text: If you sold for a reason, a higher price later isn't a new reason to buy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's a real example. In March 2000, the Nasdaq index of tech stocks peaked above five thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Over the next two and a half years, it fell about seventy-eight percent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Say you sold some tech shares in 1999, with a profit, and then watched them double.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If you bought back in at the top, ten thousand dollars became about two thousand two hundred.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Before you buy back, write down why you sold. Has that reason changed?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If the only new fact is that other people made money, that's not a reason. That's envy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And never buy back with more money than you sold, just to catch up.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the rule isn't perfect. Sometimes the price keeps rising, and buying back was right.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Even Newton held some shares that recovered a little.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Gravity always wins. Bubbles too, eventually.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: nave of Westminster Abbey, 1727: tall Gothic arches, stone floor, candles, banners, a carved monument, cool daylight
scenes.title: YOUR LIFE AS ISAAC NEWTON

titleOptions: Your Life as Isaac Newton | Genius, Mint Boss, Bubble Loser
Your Life as the Smartest Man Who Lost to a Bubble
Your Life as Isaac Newton | Hunting Counterfeiters
meta.thumbnail: A packed 1720 London coffee house with share-price boards and flying papers; text: 'LOST TO A BUBBLE'
meta.description:
It's 1720. You explained gravity, you run the Royal Mint, and you're buying back into the biggest bubble in England.
By winter, you'll have lost a fortune. This is the life of Isaac Newton.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.
General education only, not financial advice.

Sources:
- Isaac Newton, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton
- South Sea Company, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sea_Company
- Thomas Levenson, Newton and the Counterfeiter (2009)
- Andrew Odlyzko, 'Newton's financial misadventures in the South Sea Bubble', Notes and Records of the Royal Society (2019)
- Richard S. Westfall, Never at Rest (1980)
factCheck: Born 25 December 1642 (Julian; 4 January 1643 Gregorian) at Woolsthorpe; father died three months before; premature, 'fit in a quart mug'; mother married Barnabas Smith when he was three and left him with grandmother Margery Ayscough (Wikipedia).
List of sins up to age 19 (Fitzwilliam notebook, 1662) includes 'Threatening my father and mother Smith to burn them and the house over them' (Wikipedia; Westfall).
King's School Grantham from about 12, lodging with apothecary Clark; built windmill model, sundials, lantern kite (Stukeley's memoir; widely cited, details DISPUTED).

Mother pulled him out by October 1659 to farm; fined by the manor court for letting animals stray (Westfall, Never at Rest; DISPUTED in detail); schoolmaster and uncle persuaded her to send him back (Wikipedia).

Trinity College June 1661 as subsizar doing valet duties; scholarship 1664; university closed for plague 1665; worked at Woolsthorpe 1665-1667 (Wikipedia). 'Emptying chamber pots' is the usual description of sizar duties: DISPUTED.

Apple story: Stukeley's memoir of a 1726 conversation, apple fell in the garden, did not hit his head (Wikipedia). Lucasian professor 1669 aged 26; lectures sometimes to empty rooms (Humphrey Newton's account, as cited by Westfall).
Letter to Hooke, February 1675/76: 'If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants'; possible jab at Hooke's short stature is a historians' reading: DISPUTED (Wikipedia).

Halley's 1684 visit; Principia published 5 July 1687 with Halley's financial help; Royal Society had spent its funds on Willughby's De Historia Piscium (1686) and paid Halley in copies of it (Royal Society history; widely cited).
Clipping and the Great Recoinage of 1696; coins had lost close to half their weight by 1695 (Wikipedia, Great Recoinage); Gresham's law (general).

Warden of the Mint 1696 via Charles Montagu; salary about £400 a year (Westfall); estimated 20% of coins counterfeit; counterfeiting was high treason; disguise in taverns (Wikipedia, DISPUTED how often); 100+ cross-examinations June 1698-Christmas 1699; 28 coiners prosecuted; William Chaloner hanged March 1699 (Wikipedia; Levenson).
Chaloner told Parliament the Mint was badly run and offered methods to stop counterfeiting (Levenson 2009).
Master of the Mint from 1699 (Wikipedia); income often over £1,000 a year from fees on coinage (Westfall; DISPUTED by year).
Catherine Barton his half-niece kept house on Jermyn Street (Wikipedia); never married (Wikipedia). Knighted April 1705 by Queen Anne, likely for political reasons (Wikipedia).
Report of 21 September 1717; proclamation 22 December 1717 fixed the guinea at no more than 21 shillings, moving Britain to a de facto gold standard; whether intended is debated (Wikipedia).
South Sea shares rose from about £128 in January 1720 to about £1,000 in June-August, then collapsed in September to near £150 by year end (Wikipedia, South Sea Company).

Newton sold shares in spring 1720 at a profit and bought back in summer; lost at least £10,000 and plausibly over £20,000 (Wikipedia; Odlyzko 2019). Over £1.5 million today using a rough 180-200x multiplier.

'I can calculate the motions of the heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people': secondhand anecdote recorded later (Spence), attribution DISPUTED (Odlyzko 2019). Relatives' remark that he could not bear to hear of the South Sea: Spence anecdote, DISPUTED.
Died 20 March 1726/27 in Kensington, aged 84; estate about £30,000; first scientist buried in Westminster Abbey (Wikipedia).

Voltaire in London wrote Newton 'was never sensible to any passion' (Wikipedia, Letters on the English). Pope's epitaph 'Nature and Nature's laws lay hid in night: God said, Let Newton be! and all was light' (Wikipedia).
Nasdaq Composite peaked at 5,048.62 on 10 March 2000 and fell about 78% to 1,114 by 9 October 2002 (Nasdaq historical data). $10,000 at the top would have been about $2,200 at the bottom.
sources: 'Threatening my father and mother Smith to burn them and the house over them.': Newton's list of sins (1662), Fitzwilliam notebook, as quoted in Westfall, Never at Rest (1980) and Wikipedia
'If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.': Newton, letter to Robert Hooke, 5 February 1675/76
'O dear Sir, nobody can save me but you.': William Chaloner, letter to Newton, March 1699, as quoted in Levenson, Newton and the Counterfeiter (2009)
'He was never sensible to any passion.': Voltaire, Letters on the English (1733), as quoted on Wikipedia
Alexander Pope, epitaph for Newton (1730): 'God said, Let Newton be! and all was light.'
Andrew Odlyzko, 'Newton's financial misadventures in the South Sea Bubble', Notes and Records of the Royal Society 73 (2019)
